items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: someone else was the Big Man there, Talmadge or something -- Norman Talmadge -- someone like that

ctx.x: Who was it you drove your bargain with? Who was it that agreed to your terms?

Well, George Estolle really agreed to them, you know, but we were in Mr. Mayer's office; I never will forget, because we went right in there, they took me right in the Big Man's office. And someone else was the Big Man there, Talmadge or something -- Norman Talmadge -- someone like that, but MGM was really the biggest studio in Hollywood then.

And so I did that with George Estolle and them --and it did launch me as a -- it helped me immensely in the studios. But after that, I think, was when Lionel Hampton came back with Benny Goodman, when he broke up in 1940; he came out here and he formed his band, and what he wanted for the rhythm section was Nat's trio and myself, you know. And all the young musicians then just loved big bands, you know, because that's what it was, you know; Andy Kirk, Benny, and Artie Shaw, Charlie Barnet, you know --Basie and…
